verses.text: Now David was old and full of days; and he made Solomon his son king over Israel.
He gathered together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
The Levites were counted from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
David said, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of Yahweh’s house, six thousand were officers and judges,
four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised Yahweh with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three.
The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan.
The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah didn’t have many sons; therefore they became a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron was separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons, forever, to burn incense before Yahweh, to minister to him, and to bless in his name, forever.
But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
The sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only: and their brothers the sons of Kish took them as wives.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.

These were the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who were counted individually, in the number of names by their polls, who did the work for the service of Yahweh’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
For David said, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever.
Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.”
For by the last words of David the sons of Levi were counted, from twenty years old and upward.

For their office was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of Yahweh’s house, in the courts, and in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house;

for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size;
and to stand every morning to thank and praise Yahweh, and likewise in the evening;
and to offer all burnt offerings to Yahweh, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before Yahweh;
and that they should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron their brothers, for the service of Yahweh’s house.

footnotes.content: David, now old and full of days, hands the kingdom to Solomon. What grace that his final act was not to cling but to pass the torch. Even the greatest must learn the hardest lesson: to step aside and trust the Lord with what comes next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David gathers all the princes, priests, and Levites—a full assembly called to witness the change of reign. The best hand-offs happen in the open, with witnesses, so there is no doubt and no room for quarreling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty-eight thousand Levites counted, each one from thirty years old and up. The Lord sees each one—no soul is lost in the multitude, no name forgotten. That was David's comfort, and it remains ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-four thousand to oversee the house of the Lord, six thousand as officers and judges. David divided their work carefully, knowing that service to God requires order, wisdom, and many hands ready to play their part.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four thousand doorkeepers, four thousand to praise with instruments David had made. The Lord delights in praise offered from prepared hearts—when we have thought about how to sing, it shows we believe the song matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David divided the Levites into families: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari—ancient names that trace back to Levi himself. Family lines carry memory; God honors the work of fathers and mothers for generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei. Two brothers, each leading a household. The Lord loves to work through family, making brothers and sisters partners in His kingdom work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehiel the chief among Ladan's sons, along with Zetham and Joel. Names matter in Scripture—each one a person the Lord knew by heart, each one called to a purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shimei's sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, Haran—heads of fathers' households. Three brothers, three leaders. When the Lord raises up leaders, He raises up more than one so that pride cannot settle in any heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Four sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. Notice how the genealogy names repeat, yet each name belongs to a real person with a real calling. Family patterns teach us the Lord works through generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When two brothers have few sons, they join as one household for counting. The Lord makes room for small families too—no one is passed over because their branch is slender.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kohath's sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel—four brothers, each head of his line. From Kohath came Moses and Aaron; the Lord's greatest servants often come through ordinary families.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron was set apart to sanctify the most holy things and bless in Yahweh's name forever. Here is the anchor: the priesthood is not a family business but a holy calling, eternal and sacred. Moses gave the law; Aaron gives intercession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses the man of God—his sons are named among Levi, not set apart for priesthood like Aaron's. The greatest teacher's sons became part of the Levite work. Greatness in one generation does not demand priesthood in the next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gershom and Eliezer, sons of Moses. Two boys born to a man called to lead a nation. Moses served God; his sons served in the tabernacle. That is faithfulness lived out in quieter ways.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shebuel was chief of Gershom's line. Leadership passes, names are remembered, work continues. The Lord's kingdom moves like a relay, hand to hand, from age to age.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rehabiah, chief of Eliezer's line, had many sons though Eliezer had only one. The Lord blesses one generation sparsely and the next abundantly. We cannot always see His pattern, but we can trust it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shelomith, chief of Izhar's sons. Another name, another household, another corner of the work assigned and honored. The Lord fills His house with many servants.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hebron's sons: Jeriah the chief, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, Jekameam fourth. Four leaders in birth order—a reminder that seniority meant something. Respect for order is respect for God's design.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Uzziel's sons: Micah the chief, Isshiah second. Two brothers, two chiefs, two lines of service. The Lord delights in multiplying leaders, not hoarding authority.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Merari's sons: Mahli and Mushi. These names trace all the way back to Levi—three families, three pillars holding up the work. The Lord builds His house on solid family foundations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eleazar died childless; his daughters married their cousins. Kindness kept the family whole and the inheritance safe. Love finds a way even when death tries to divide.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mahli, Eder, Jeremoth—three sons of Mushi. Every name written, every line honored, every household counted. The Lord's scribe never makes a mistake or forgets a soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From twenty years old and up, they did the service of the Lord's house. This was David's final gift: a clear order, a recorded genealogy, a structure that outlasted him. Wise leaders build what remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh has given rest to His people; He dwells in Jerusalem forever. David speaks as an old man who has seen war end, the enemy subdued, the temple site chosen. Rest comes when we stop fighting and let the Lord sit down.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No longer would the Levites carry the tabernacle and its vessels. For centuries they bore the burden of a tent moving from place to place; now they settle in service around a house. Sometimes blessing looks like permission to rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By David's last words, the Levites were counted from twenty years old. Even in his final days, David's concern was order, clarity, and the preparation of God's house. Legacy is what we leave prepared.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Levites waited on Aaron's sons in the courts, rooms, and purifying of holy things. A hundred different tasks, but one purpose: to keep the house of God clean and holy. Service is never small when it serves the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Show bread, fine flour, meal offerings—every detail counted, every measurement watched. The Lord receives not just our hearts but our careful hands and orderly minds. Precision in service is a form of love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To thank and praise Yahweh every morning and evening. The rhythm of daily praise—beginning and ending with the Lord—that was the Levite's life. A life framed by thanksgiving is a life that never forgets whom it serves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: the offering on Sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts. We no longer carry the tabernacle or burn sacrifices, yet the rhythm remains—the Lord still calls us to mark time with Him, to pause and remember. As of 2026-10, I'm grateful He still invites us to gather, to worship, to break bread in His presence at His table.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the holy place, and serve Aaron's brothers. One people, many duties, one God—that was the priesthood's calling. Today it remains: the Lord invites all His people to serve in the place where His name dwells.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
